title: Termination of a while loop by a variant
statement: Let a program execute under limits and at recursion depth $d$, and consider a while loop with guard $c$ and body $s$, starting in state $\sigma$. Suppose an invariant $I$ holds initially, and whenever $I$ holds the guard is safe. Whenever $I$ holds and the guard is true, the body terminates within cost $b$, preserves $I$, and strictly decreases a natural-valued measure $m$. Whenever $I$ holds and the guard is false, a postcondition $Q$ holds. If $m(\sigma)(\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+b)+\operatorname{cost}(c)+1\le T$, then the loop terminates within cost $T$ and its final state satisfies $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: Initial invariant holds at the starting state
The guard is safe at every state satisfying the invariant
When the invariant and guard hold, the body terminates within cost b, preserves the invariant, and strictly decreases m
When the invariant holds and the guard is false, Q holds
Initial measure times (guard cost plus 1 plus b), plus guard cost plus 1, is at most T
